title: Repeating Hurtful Relationships: Why Do I Keep Choosing the Same Person?
description: Why do I keep ending up in the same hurtful relationship? On familiarity, fear of being alone and self-worth, with an exercise to understand your choices.
image_alt: A young woman sitting on a chair facing three young men who all cast the same shadow
summary: Repeating the same hurtful relationship doesn't mean you're stupid, weak or just “unlucky”; there may be a pattern worth understanding. Familiar doesn't mean right for you, and intermittent affection, fear of being alone and the way we see ourselves can all make leaving harder. Understanding your choices doesn't make you responsible for someone else's harm; responsibility for harm lies with the person causing it.

title: The Four Attachment Styles: How They Differ and Shape Relationships
description: A clear guide to secure, anxious, avoidant and fearful-avoidant attachment, with a comparison, examples, an exercise, sources and the limits of self-tests.
image_alt: A young woman reaching out her hand to a young man who walks away with a cloud over his head
summary: Attachment styles describe differences in how safe and close we feel in relationships. Common categories include secure, anxious, avoidant and fearful-avoidant. They're descriptions that help understanding — not diagnoses or fixed identities — and they can change with awareness, safe relationships and therapy.
